title: Target distribution characterisation
objective: Determine the distributional shape of performance_rating and check for subpopulations.

steps: Load dataset.csv and extract performance_rating column.
Plot histogram with 30 bins overlaid with KDE curve.
Run Shapiro-Wilk normality test; report W statistic and p-value.
Compute skewness and kurtosis.
Optionally run Hartigan dip test for unimodality.

expected_outputs.description: Histogram + KDE of performance_rating
Distribution statistics: mean, std, skew, kurtosis, Shapiro-Wilk W, p-value

validation.check: Mean should be approximately 50.0, std approximately 10.0 per profile.

title: Feature distribution overview
objective: Visualise marginal distributions for all features to identify anomalies, skew, or unexpected patterns.

steps: Load dataset.csv.
For each numeric column, plot histogram + KDE (subplot grid).
For salary_band, plot bar chart of level frequencies.
Flag any features with extreme skew (|skew| > 2) or unexpected ranges.

expected_outputs.description: Grid of histograms for all features
Bar chart of salary_band frequencies

validation.check: All feature ranges should match column_summary.csv min/max values.

title: Linear correlation analysis
objective: Compute Pearson correlations between each numeric feature and performance_rating.

steps: Load dataset; select numeric columns excluding employee_id.
Compute Pearson r and p-value for each feature vs performance_rating using scipy.stats.pearsonr.
Build a full correlation matrix heatmap for all numeric features.
Record all individual p-values for later FDR correction in EXP-11.

expected_outputs.description: Full pairwise Pearson correlation heatmap
Feature, Pearson r, p-value for each feature vs performance_rating

validation.check: Correlation values must be in [-1, 1]; p-values in [0, 1]. If data is pure noise, expect |r| < 0.1 for most pairs.

title: Nonlinear association detection
objective: Test for nonlinear relationships using Spearman rank correlation and distance correlation.

steps: Compute Spearman rho and p-value for each numeric feature vs performance_rating.
Compute distance correlation (dcor library or manual) for each feature vs performance_rating.
Generate scatter plots with LOWESS smoother for each feature vs performance_rating.
Record all p-values for FDR correction in EXP-11.

expected_outputs.description: Scatter plots with LOWESS for each feature vs performance_rating
Feature, Spearman rho, p-value, distance correlation for each feature vs performance_rating

validation.check: If distance correlation is near zero for all features, confirms lack of any (linear or nonlinear) association.

title: Performance rating by salary band
objective: Test whether performance_rating differs across salary_band groups.

steps: Group dataset by salary_band; compute group means, medians, and standard deviations for performance_rating.
Run Kruskal-Wallis H-test across groups.
Generate box plots of performance_rating by salary_band.
If Kruskal-Wallis is significant, run post-hoc Dunn test with Bonferroni correction.
Record Kruskal-Wallis p-value for FDR correction in EXP-11.

expected_outputs.description: Box plots of performance_rating by salary_band
Group statistics and Kruskal-Wallis H, p-value

validation.check: Each salary_band group should have at least 100 observations based on profile (top=L5, freq=170).

title: Multicollinearity assessment
objective: Check pairwise correlations and VIF among numeric predictors.

steps: Compute full Pearson correlation matrix for numeric features (excluding employee_id and performance_rating).
Plot annotated heatmap.
Compute VIF for each predictor using statsmodels.
Flag any predictor with VIF > 5 or any pair with |r| > 0.5.

expected_outputs.description: Correlation heatmap of predictors only
Feature, VIF value for each predictor

validation.check: If features are independently generated, expect all VIF near 1.0 and all |r| < 0.1.

title: Linear regression baseline comparison
objective: Fit OLS regression and compare cross-validated performance to a mean-prediction baseline.

steps: Define features: all numeric columns except employee_id and performance_rating. Target: performance_rating.
Compute baseline RMSE (std of target) and baseline R-squared (0.0).
Fit OLS linear regression using 5-fold cross-validation.
Record mean CV RMSE and R-squared.
Report OLS F-test p-value from full-sample fit.
Record F-test p-value for FDR correction in EXP-11.

expected_outputs.description: Model, CV RMSE, CV R-squared, F-test p-value
Bar chart comparing baseline vs OLS vs random forest RMSE and R-squared

validation.check: Baseline RMSE should be approximately 10.0 (target std). OLS RMSE should be close to or above baseline if no signal.

title: Random forest with permutation test
objective: Fit a random forest regressor and use a permutation test to assess whether predictive power is genuine.

steps: Define same features and target as EXP-07.
Fit RandomForestRegressor (100 trees, max_depth=5) with 5-fold CV. Record RMSE and R-squared.
Extract feature importances from full-sample fit.
Run permutation test: shuffle target 100 times, refit 5-fold CV each time, collect null R-squared distribution.
Compute permutation p-value: proportion of null R-squared >= observed R-squared.
Plot histogram of null R-squared distribution with observed value marked.
Record permutation p-value for FDR correction in EXP-11.

expected_outputs.description: Null R-squared distribution with observed value line
Bar chart of random forest feature importances
RF CV RMSE, R-squared, permutation p-value

validation.check: Permutation p-value should be > 0.05 if data is pure noise. If p < 0.05, genuine signal may exist.

title: Salary band classification
objective: Test whether salary_band is predictable from numeric features vs majority-class baseline.

steps: Define features: all numeric columns except employee_id. Target: salary_band.
Compute majority-class baseline accuracy (max class frequency / 800).
Fit RandomForestClassifier (100 trees) with 5-fold CV. Record accuracy, macro F1.
Generate confusion matrix from cross-validated predictions.
Run binomial test: observed accuracy vs baseline probability.
Record binomial test p-value for FDR correction in EXP-11.

expected_outputs.description: Confusion matrix heatmap
Baseline accuracy, RF accuracy, macro F1, binomial p-value

validation.check: Baseline accuracy should be approximately 21.25% (170/800). If RF accuracy is close to baseline, salary_band is unpredictable.

title: PCA and cluster analysis
objective: Search for natural employee segments using dimensionality reduction and clustering.

steps: Standardize all numeric features (exclude employee_id).
Run PCA; plot scree plot of explained variance by component.
Scatter plot of first two PCs, coloured by salary_band.
Run K-Means for k=2..6; compute silhouette score for each k.
Plot silhouette scores vs k.
For best k, compute adjusted Rand index between cluster labels and salary_band.
Compare silhouette scores to reference values from shuffled (uniform random) data.

expected_outputs.description: PCA scree plot (explained variance per component)
PCA scatter of first two components, coloured by salary_band
Silhouette score vs number of clusters
k, silhouette score, adjusted Rand index vs salary_band

validation.check: If data is pure noise, PCA variance should be roughly uniform across components and silhouette scores should be low (< 0.25).

title: Multiple-comparison correction (FDR)
objective: Apply Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction to all p-values collected from previous experiments.

steps: Collect all p-values from: Pearson correlations (EXP-03), Spearman correlations (EXP-04), Kruskal-Wallis (EXP-05), OLS F-test (EXP-07), permutation test (EXP-08), binomial test (EXP-09).
Apply Benjamini-Hochberg procedure at alpha=0.05 using statsmodels.stats.multitest.multipletests.
Report original p-values, adjusted p-values, and reject/fail-to-reject decisions.
Summarize: count of tests that survive correction out of total tests.

expected_outputs.description: Test ID, source experiment, original p-value, BH-adjusted p-value, reject null (yes/no)

validation.check: Total number of p-values should equal the number of individual tests run. If zero survive, conclude no detectable signal in the dataset.
